title: Adding, Updating, and Removing Elements
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of adding, updating, and removing elements in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply adding, updating, and removing elements in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to in-place modifications and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Adding, Updating, and Removing Elements through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding adding, updating, and removing elements helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Adding, Updating, and Removing Elements helps you reason about push , << , and unshift. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: push , << , and unshift. Then connect it to pop and shift. The remaining syllabus points—delete and delete_at, In-place modifications—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports adding, updating, and removing elements. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a second example for adding, updating, and removing elements using a different input. Add one edge case from the syllabus list (In-place modifications), state the expected behavior, and write a small test or manual check that would catch a regression.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain adding, updating, and removing elements, identify its place in arrays, run a focused example, and verify an important boundary. Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
